Definition: from G2596 and G2744; to exult against (i.e. over):--boast (against), glory, rejoice against.
BiblicalUsage: To boast against is to exult over someone, and Paul tells the Gentiles not to boast against the branches, while James says mercy rejoices against judgment and bitter envying should not glory against the truth. The word always picks a side: pride against the other branch, or mercy against the sentence. One is forbidden and the other is the gospel.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe boasting against my brother forgets that I am a branch grafted in by grace, not a root holding myself up. I hold that mercy is the only boasting that is safe, because it rejoices against judgment and leaves the last word to God.
